summary: Three independent backend runs exercised authentication, invitations, tenant isolation, CRUD, scheduling, LHU storage/evaluation, dashboard/compliance/trends, WhatsApp settings, reminders, notifications, cron authorization, and file access. Core flows generally worked, but the union found cross-tenant reference validation defects (foreign site and lab IDs), client-controlled LHU compliance limits, missing brute-force protection, CORS configuration/security problems, unreliable background email delivery, insecure admin credential fallback, and blocking synchronous storage I/O in async handlers. Frontend was not tested because the request was backend-only. All three runs were reachable and returned usable findings. Checked-working coverage included Bearer auth/me, company and invitation lifecycle with single-use tokens, CRUD, month-end due dates, LHU upload/download/list/soft-delete, dashboard/compliance/trend, WhatsApp masking, reminders/notifications, cron secret enforcement, and query-level cross-company read/write isolation.

critical.title: Monitoring point update accepts a site owned by another company
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Login as company A admin and company B admin; create a site in B and a monitoring point in A; PUT the A point with company_id=A and site_id=B's site ID, keeping all other fields valid.
critical.expected: Reject the update with 400/403 and preserve the A point's existing site association because the target site is not owned by company A.
critical.actual: The request returned 200 and persisted/changed the A point's site_id to company B's site ID.
critical.impact: Tenant data can be cross-linked and corrupted through site/monitoring-point relationships, violating row-level isolation and data integrity.

critical.title: LHU upload accepts a lab ID belonging to another company
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Login as admins for companies A and B; create a point in A and lab in B; upload an LHU for A's point while passing B's lab_id.
critical.expected: Reject the foreign lab_id with 400/403; only a lab belonging to the selected company should be accepted.
critical.actual: The request returned 200 and persisted the B lab_id on A's LHU record.
critical.impact: Cross-tenant references can enter compliance records and leak or corrupt lab attribution.

critical.title: LHU result evaluation trusts client-supplied baku mutu instead of monitoring-point configuration
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Create a monitoring-point parameter such as pH with a stored baku_mutu limit (for example 8 or 9), then upload a result above that limit while omitting the limit or supplying a permissive client-supplied baku_mutu in the results JSON.
critical.expected: Evaluate against the monitoring point's stored parameter limits and mark the over-limit result melebihi.
critical.actual: The implementation passes raw client JSON directly to _evaluate_results, so the submitted/missing limit can cause an over-limit value to be marked sesuai.
critical.impact: Users can forge limits and obtain false compliance results, affecting compliance scores, trends, and audit integrity.

critical.title: No brute-force lockout or throttling after repeated failed logins
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Submit five or six consecutive invalid-password requests for alfianfahrur@gmail.com, then submit the correct password.
critical.expected: After the configured failure threshold, throttle or temporarily lock the account/source and return a lockout/rate-limit response such as 423/429; the valid login should remain blocked during the lockout.
critical.actual: All failed attempts returned 401 and the correct login returned 200 immediately after the failures; no lockout or throttling was observed.
critical.impact: Admin and user accounts remain vulnerable to online password guessing and credential stuffing.

critical.title: CORS reflects arbitrary origins while allowing credentials
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Send an OPTIONS request with Origin=https://evil.example, Access-Control-Request-Method=GET, and Access-Control-Request-Headers=authorization.
critical.expected: Only configured trusted origins should be allowed when credentials are enabled.
critical.actual: The response returned 200 with access-control-allow-origin=https://evil.example and access-control-allow-credentials=true; backend/.env sets CORS_ORIGINS="*".
critical.impact: Any origin can make credentialed browser requests to the API, weakening tenant and authentication boundary protections.

critical.title: CORS preflight returns a different origin than the public frontend origin
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Send an OPTIONS request to the public backend URL with Origin=https://lhu-vault.preview.emergentagent.com.
critical.expected: Access-Control-Allow-Origin should equal the requesting configured frontend origin.
critical.actual: The response returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin=https://lhu-vault.cluster-5.preview.emergentcf.cloud instead of the public frontend origin.
critical.impact: Browser requests from the configured frontend origin may be blocked by CORS, preventing API integration in deployed browser sessions.

minor.title: Invitation and reminder email delivery is unreliable in background tasks
minor.location: POST /api/companies, POST /api/invitations, POST /api/reminders/run-now; background _send_invite_email and run_reminder_check
minor.steps_to_reproduce: Create/invite test users and execute reminders while monitoring backend logs and notification statuses.
minor.expected: Email sends should succeed or failures should be retried and clearly surfaced without treating the API request as successful.
minor.actual: The APIs returned 200, but logs recorded repeated provider 422 and 429 responses and notification entries with gagal status; failures were logged asynchronously and not reliably surfaced. The 429 component may be amplified by concurrent test activity.
minor.impact: Invitees and compliance recipients may not receive access links or due-date reminders despite successful API responses.

minor.title: Admin seed uses insecure fallback credentials when environment variables are absent
minor.steps_to_reproduce: Run startup without ADMIN_EMAIL or ADMIN_PASSWORD configured.
minor.expected: Startup should fail fast because administrator credentials are required from environment variables.
minor.actual: The code falls back to admin@example.com/admin123 and seeds an account.
minor.impact: A deployment with missing configuration could expose a predictable administrator account.

minor.title: Synchronous object-storage HTTP calls run inside async request handlers
minor.steps_to_reproduce: Review the LHU upload/download handlers and storage_service.put_object/get_object calls.
minor.expected: Blocking storage I/O should be async or moved off the event loop.
minor.actual: The async FastAPI handlers call synchronous requests-based storage methods directly.
minor.impact: Concurrent LHU uploads/downloads can block the event loop and reduce API responsiveness.

action_items: Validate site_id ownership against the selected company on monitoring-point updates.
Validate lab_id ownership against the selected company before persisting an LHU.
Derive LHU evaluation limits exclusively from stored monitoring-point parameters, never client-supplied limits.
Add account/IP failure tracking with lockout or rate limiting after repeated failed logins.
Restrict credentialed CORS to an explicit trusted-origin allowlist and ensure the deployed public frontend origin is configured.
Handle email-provider failures with retries and an explicit surfaced delivery state.
Remove predictable administrator credential fallbacks and fail fast when required environment variables are missing.
Move blocking object-storage calls off async request handlers or use an async client.
